mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate directly reduces the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of other conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 5.0% in a 3-month window, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5d returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS decline by >1%.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansions (FEDFUNDS > 3.0% and UNRATE < 4.0%), aggressive monetary tightening reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60d returns are positive in more than 50% of instances meeting the regime condition.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals robust manufacturing activity and economic growth, supporting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO rises by >0.5% monthly.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1800.0 thousand units, it indicates a weakening housing market and reduced consumer confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5d returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when HOUST < 1800.0.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in payroll growth (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a deteriorating labor market, reducing consumer spending and corporate profits, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are positive in more than 45% of instances where PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises.

mechanism_narrative: Strong retail sales (RSAFS) indicate robust consumer spending, supporting corporate revenue growth and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of other conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when RSAFS exceeds its 12-month moving average.
